translations.text: Paul, a servant of God and an apostle of Jesus Christ, according to the faith of God's elect and by the knowledge of the truth, which belongs to the service of God,
by the hope of eternal life, which God who does not lie promised us before those eternal times,
and his word was revealed in its own times through the preaching that was entrusted to me by the command of God our Savior,
to Titus, a true son according to the common faith: grace and peace from God the Father and from Jesus Christ our Savior.
For this reason I left you in Crete, so that you might set in order what was lacking and appoint elders in city after city, as I commanded you:
whoever is blameless, the husband of one wife; let him have believing children, and let them not be accused of filthiness or disobedience.
For a bishop must be blameless and spotless, as a steward of God, not self-willed, nor quick-tempered, not a wine-drinker, not a brawler, not one who acquires shameful gain,
but a lover of guests, a lover of good, chaste, righteous, worthy of respect, patient, holding firmly, in keeping with the teaching,
to the word of faith, so that he may be able both to give comfort in the teaching of life and to reprove those who contradict.
For there are many who are insubordinate, speakers of vanity, deceivers of the mind, especially those of the circumcision,
whose mouths must be struck, who overturn whole households, teaching what ought not to be taught for the sake of shameful gain.
One of them, their own prophet, said: Cretans are always liars, evil beasts, idle bellies.
This testimony is true. For this reason reprove them unsparingly, so that they may be alive in the faith,
not heeding Jewish fables and the commandment of men who have turned away from the truth.
All things are pure for the pure; but for the defiled and unbelieving nothing is pure, but both their heart and their mind are defiled.
They profess that they know God, but by their deeds they deny him; they are abominable and disobedient and unproven for every good deed.
But as for you, speak what befits the teaching of life:
let the elders be vigilant, worthy of respect, chaste, alive in faith, in love, in patience;
let the aged women likewise be beautiful in quietness, not slanderers, not subject to much wine, but teachers of what is good,
so that they may instruct the young women to love their husbands, to love their children,
to be chaste, spotless, keepers of the house, kind, subject to their own husbands, so that the word of God may not be blasphemed.
Likewise exhort the young men to be chaste.
Before all, offer yourself as a pattern through good deeds, with incorruptibility and dignity in your teaching,
a living and irreproachable word, so that the opponent may be ashamed and have nothing evil to say against us.
Let slaves be subject to their own masters, let them be pleasing in everything, not contradicting.
Let them not pilfer, but let them show all good faith, so that they may adorn the teaching of God our Savior in everything.
For the grace of God has appeared as Savior to all people,
to instruct us, so that we may renounce ungodliness and the desire of the world, and live in purity and righteousness and godliness in this world,
and await that blessed hope and the manifestation of the glory of the great God and our Savior Jesus Christ,
who gave himself for us, so that he might redeem us from all lawlessness and purify for himself a people acquired as his own, emulators of good works.
Say these things, and exhort and reprove with all authority. Let no one despise you.
Remind them to submit to rulers and authorities, to be obedient, and to be ready for every good work,
to slander no one, to be free of contention and kind, showing all gentleness toward all people.
For we too were once ignorant and disobedient and led astray, and we were slaves to many desires and pleasures; we lived in wickedness and envy, hateful and hating one another.
But when the kindness and love for humankind of God our Savior appeared,
not from works of righteousness that we had done, but by his mercy he saved us, through the washing of rebirth and the renewal of the Holy Spirit,
which he poured out on us richly through Jesus Christ our Savior,
so that we might be justified by his grace and become heirs of the hope of eternal life.
The word is trustworthy; and concerning these things I want you to affirm firmly, so that these who believe in God may take care to excel in good works. This is good and profitable for people.
But keep away from foolish inquiries and empty words and disputes and quarrels about the law, for they are unprofitable and vain.
As for the heretical man, avoid him after one or two instructions.
Know that such a person is perverted and sins, and is condemned by his own self.
When I send Artemas or Tychicus to you, hasten to come to me at Nicopolis, for I have chosen to spend the winter there.
Send Zenas the lawyer and Apollos on their way quickly, so that they may lack nothing.
Let our people also learn to devote themselves to good works for the sake of unavoidable needs, so that they may not be unfruitful.
All who are with me greet you. Give greetings to those who love us in faith. Grace be with you all. Amen.
